display_name: Provision a managed role session on request
description: The registered process returns an accepted job receipt in data.job_id and data.status=queued. Retain that exact canonical id and read service_interface::job_service::get_job until terminal. The stored job.result is the original operation envelope, including data and structured error; job.error is also retained on failure. A receipt does not establish a session, dispatch row, or successful first turn. launch_busy names the current operation/job and starts no work. One-call composition for a requested named role session. It reads an existing role row first and honors its role_class; an unrecognized name defaults to project so callers do not need to know that Git-Controller is project-class. Only an explicitly requested, as-yet-unlegislated principal is legislated, and that governance act stays visible in the result. It then reuses spawn_session's local-name resolution and managed-dispatch path. The spawned worker receives the normal first-turn instruction to claim its own durable role binding; this verb never claims or evicts a holder on the worker's behalf.
embedding_description: Submit a bounded session-launch job and retrieve its final result by exact job id. Provision a named project or principal role session without making the caller guess role class. Use for Git-Controller on request; defaults new names to project, legislates only a requested principal, and lets the worker claim itself.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Accepted submission only: data.job_id and data.status=queued. After terminal retrieval, job.result.data carries the original operation fields; job.result.error preserves its error. Continue dependent actions only after this retrieval.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report acceptance with job_id. Retrieve the terminal job before reporting an instance, dispatch state, first-turn outcome, or qualification verdict. Keep uptake_pending and uptake_uncertain distinct from worker ACK.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Class resolution and authorization happen before legislation or managed dispatch. A principal legislation occurs only for an explicit requested principal with no existing role row; project roles are not legislated.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument means role_name was empty. unknown_role_class means requested_role_class was not empty, project, or principal. role_class_not_spawn_assignable means the existing role row carries a class that spawn_session cannot assign. Authorization and dispatch failures retain their existing precise errors.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For a standard project role such as Git-Controller, omit requested_role_class. Specify principal only when the caller intentionally requests a new principal office; resolve dispatch or launcher configuration failures using the exact returned detail.
